data.title: Dependency
data.tagline: External code packages a project declares it will use, usually installed from its manifest by a package manager
data.learningOutcome: You can tell whether a missing-module error means dependencies were never installed, the version is wrong, or the code itself is broken.
data.description: After cloning a project, package.json declares its dependencies and a lockfile records resolved versions; the package manager prepares a local install directory from them. Repositories usually do not commit node_modules. If you see Cannot find module, first check whether dependencies were installed, then start the project as documented and inspect the actual error.

learning.assumes: You have seen projects require an install step, or hit a missing-module error.
learning.outcome: You can tell whether a missing-module error means dependencies were never installed, the version is wrong, or the code itself is broken.

distinctions.label: npm
distinctions.explanation: npm is the tool that installs and manages dependencies; a dependency is one of the packages it installs into the project.

distinctions.label: Your own source code
distinctions.explanation: Dependencies are external packages declared and resolved by the package manager; your own files belong to the project repository. Changes to either may need a rebuild or refresh before they appear.

explanation.title: The project stores a list, not the packages
explanation.text: The repository usually tracks a manifest and may track a lockfile; the install directory is commonly generated locally rather than committed.

explanation.title: Installing prepares the local dependency directory
explanation.text: The package manager reads the manifest and lockfile, downloads or reuses required packages, and prepares a local install directory. A fresh clone or dependency change usually needs installation as documented by the project.

explanation.title: Errors map to different causes
explanation.text: Cannot find module first suggests dependencies were never installed. If it persists after installing, check the version match and whether the import path is wrong.

data.boundary: A successful install does not mean the project runs: versions must still match and configuration must be complete. When installation fails, identify which package failed and why before retrying or adjusting versions.

lessonPractice.title: A newly cloned project reports Cannot find module 'react' when running npm start. What should happen next?

options.label: Run npm install first, then start the project again
options.feedback: Correct. A cloned project usually contains the dependency records, not the packages themselves. Installing first is the normal flow.

options.label: Ask AI to rewrite the code without importing react
options.feedback: The error says dependencies are missing, not that the code is wrong; removing imports breaks the feature.

options.label: Reinstall Node.js because a missing module is an environment problem
options.feedback: When Node.js exists, install the project's dependencies first; a missing node itself produces a different error (command not found).

data.agentPrompt: The freshly cloned project reports Cannot find module. Run the dependency install command first, confirm every package in the manifest is installed, then start again. If installation fails, explain which package failed and why instead of working around it in business code.
